chapters.name: India: Relief Features
chapters.overview: In comparison to the Gangetic plains, the plateau region is dry. The eastern most boundary of the Himalayas is the Brahmaputra valley. Eastern Ghats and Nilgiris form of above plateaus with that of Tibetan plateau.

chapters.name: Ideas of Development
chapters.overview: However, for comparison between countries, total income is not such a useful measure. Countries with higher income are more developed than countries with lower income. Income and per capita income, though very often used, is only one aspect of development.

chapters.name: Production and Employment
chapters.overview: GDP is made up of production from the three sectors – agriculture, industry and services. People engaged in various economic activities in the above sectors produce a large number of goods and services. Production (in industry and services) has increased without a similar increase in employment.

chapters.name: Indian Rivers and Water Resources
chapters.overview: Some regions depend on rainfall and underground water (wells and tube wells). Water flowing out via surface flows and groundwater: Imagine a region such as a village. Today, this is the major source of water for people.

chapters.name: The Population
chapters.overview: The third component of population change is migration. Population density is calculated as the number of persons per unit area. Population density Population density provides a better picture of its distribution.

chapters.name: Settlements - Migrations
chapters.overview: Only one-fifth of the growth is due to rural - to - urban migration. Most of the population increase in cities and towns took place as a consequence of natural growth within the urban areas. We have examined the statistics of rural – urban migration and the multiple reasons for migration.

chapters.name: Rampur: A Village Economy
chapters.overview: Most small farmers have to borrow money to arrange for the working capital. Each worker is providing the necessary labour for production. This, in turn, means that the farmers require a sufficient amount of capital for production, and therefore money.

chapters.name: Globalisation
chapters.overview: These organisations believe that barriers to foreign trade and investment are harmful. How is it Distinguish between foreign trade and foreign investment. The Indian government, after Independence, had put barriers to foreign trade and foreign investment.

chapters.name: Food Security
chapters.overview: Increasing foodgrain production Producing sufficient amount of foodgrains is an important requirement for food security. It is not sufficient to produce foodgrains and other items. Farmers producing foodgrains can go for crop diversification in order to increase their incomes.

chapters.name: Sustainable Development with Equity
chapters.overview: Because of modern development projects, they have lost access to their greatest resource, the local environment. There is another function that the environment provides. Millets were the obvious crop choice because of their suitability to the local environment.

chapters.name: World Between the World Wars
chapters.overview: But the Russian economy had suffered a lot by the first World War. This was the immediate cause of the First World War. The Russian Socialist Revolution (1917-1922) Russia was ruled by Tsars (emperors) in early 20th century.

chapters.name: National Liberation Movements in the Colonies
chapters.overview: Manchu dynasty was unsuccessful in defending the interests of China from the western colonial powers. Even independent countries like China were actually under the control of many colonial powers and independent only in name. These powers had become very powerful and influential in different parts of China.

chapters.name: National Movement in India - Partition and Independence: 1939-1947
chapters.overview: The Congress won 26 out of the 58 Muslim seats it had contested. Congress party had never accepted the “two-nation theory”. The Congress was unable to fulfill the demands of M A Jinnah, leader of the Muslim League.

chapters.name: The Making of Independent India's Constitution
chapters.overview: The Constitution of India was prepared and adopted by the Constituent Assembly. What the Draft Constitution proposes is the Parliamentary system. Princely States were identified through ourselves this Constitution.

chapters.name: Election Process in India
chapters.overview: General Elections are conducted for every 5 years at national/state level. To conduct and monitor elections in every constituency, an officer is appointed. Political parties in Elections A political party is formed when it has a written code of conduct and registers at the Election Commission.

chapters.name: Independent India: The First 30 Years (1947-77)
chapters.overview: Yet, the Congress under Indira Gandhi was making new promises. This inaugurated what some observers called the Congress System. The Congress party formed the government in many of the states as well.

chapters.name: Emerging Political Trends 1977 to 2000
chapters.overview: Assam (Assom) Movement A similar but much stronger demand for autonomy was also taking place in Assom. It began with the state of Emergency in which basic democratic rights were denied and ended with the historic electoral victory of the Congress led by Rajiv Gandhi. This also allowed many different political viewpoints and sectional interests to become active in state level as well as national politics.

chapters.name: Post-War World and India
chapters.overview: India was one of the first countries to recognise China’s Communist government. These were to determine India’s relations with other countries, especially its neighbours – China, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and subsequently, Bangladesh. India helped China take part in Bandung conference in spite of their ideological differences.

chapters.name: Social Movements in Our Times
chapters.overview: One of the most important movements was the American Civil Rights Movement. These movements for human rights had many shades of differences. Women have been at the forefront of many important social movements in the recent past.

chapters.name: The Movement for the Formation of Telangana State
chapters.overview: At that time, Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema regions were parts of Madras Presidency. All areas of the state of Andhra Pradesh were treated as one. There were three distinct regions which spoke Telugu language.
